what: Schema encode and decode of 100000 CTAP2 getAssertion responses into and out of LMDB by reflection, with variable fields (spans) against fixed fields (std::array, credential ID 32, user handle 32, authData 37, Ed25519 signature 64). ns per record.
why: The owner asked whether LMDB with CBOR structs comes close to plain C++, and whether fixed sizes make the write faster.
how: Google Benchmark, one binary per arm, each arm built twice (a and b) for the noise floor. 3 rounds alternating, each with --benchmark_repetitions=5 --benchmark_enable_random_interleaving=true. encode_memory: cbor::encode of all records into one span. lmdb_write: a new env per iteration (timing paused for create and delete), one write txn, mdb_put with MDB_APPEND|MDB_RESERVE through a writer whose allocate returns the reserved span, one commit. lmdb_read: one read txn, cursor over all records, cbor::decode<T> of each value from the mmap. Env flags MDB_WRITEMAP|MDB_NOSYNC|MDB_NOMETASYNC, MDB_INTEGERKEY.
finding: Fixed fields: encode 26 ns against 48, LMDB write 132 against 188, LMDB read 34 against 42. The noise between a and b is under 1 ns. Of the 132 ns of a fixed write, encode is 26; the rest is LMDB.
